sentence: This project tries to lower cancer cases and deaths in rural communities by studying risk factors and testing ways to prevent cancer.
This project studies how different versions of a gene linked to brain development disorders affect human synapse development, using long-read sequencing and human cell models.
This project builds CRISPR gene editing treatments that remove disease-causing repeated DNA from genes behind neurodegenerative diseases.
This project studies why pancreatic cancer resists immune therapy differently in males and females and tests treatments that target a protein on macrophages.
This project develops drugs that target rare gene changes linked to healthy aging in people who live extremely long lives.
This project studies how two small proteins keep the genome stable and hold back viral and plasmid machinery.
This project holds a conference where researchers share how aquatic animals are used as models to study human disease.
This project tries to control opioid signaling in specific brain circuits so that pain relief from opioid drugs can be separated from dependence.
This project studies how certain cells turn into beige fat and pass mitochondria to muscle to help it regenerate.
This project studies how mutations in a gene that changes chromatin cause intellectual disability, using animal models and human cerebral organoids.
This project tries to find out why a gene family that often fails to kill cells has lasted across many organisms.
This project tests in mice and humans with obesity whether and how weight loss medications called incretin mimetics affect endometrial and colorectal cancers.
This project supports research on the causes and treatment of respiratory disease and critical illness.
This project studies how immunosuppression medications change uterine natural killer cells in people with a uterus transplant, and how this affects pregnancy.
This project uses published metagenomic data to study how the human microbiome relates to cancer.
This project studies how two families of cell surface proteins guide specific connections between nerve cells in Drosophila motor circuits.
This project studies the physical and molecular properties of large extracellular vesicles one at a time, using microfluidic technology.
This project builds a platform and computer methods to find T-cell receptors that recognize bacteria and viruses.
This project gives data management and statistical support to cancer research projects and keeps a shared data repository.
This project provides a vibratome that cuts tissue sections so researchers can study disease at the cellular level.
